title: Fixed contrasts reduced shared-release model noise across two adult worm brain maps
abstract: We tested whether low-noise input contrasts transfer between two adult C. elegans brain maps. In a model with independent sites, equal release probabilities and positive unit gains, shared site release and independent contact release have the same mean inputs and single-target variances. Ten contrasts chosen in one map gave shared-to-independent total variance ratios of 0.5989 and 0.6068 in the other map, with fixed cell weights. The primary panel had 132 targets with input in all eight developmental maps. Both test ratios were below all 999 test-label permutations within broad cell types. An adult-only panel of 160 targets gave ratios of 0.6915 and 0.6100. High-noise contrasts transferred above ratio one. Exact site calculations and Bernoulli simulation checks agreed. These are conditional variance results, not measured release noise or evidence for better coding. Partial anatomy, only two adult animals, unknown release dependence and untested signal directions limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records and derived cell-level files are excluded from the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Fixed contrasts chosen in one adult map retain reduced shared-release model variance in another map. The figure shows panel and dimension checks and within-type label references. These are model results, not measured neural noise.

citations.reason: Uses the shared-release model and panel definition as prior context. Tests fixed contrasts across maps instead of separate fitted extrema. No prior code or record tables are bundled.
Prior joint-delivery model; the present study tests transfer of linear variance contrasts.
